title: Beverage Element Standing on a Final Event Bill
content:
The bar element standing on a Private Event & Banquet Services final bill follows the room the booking was taken for and the guests served.

1. Where that room stood set for a reception and the guests served reach the smallest guest count printed against the package, the bar minimum printed against the package stands on the bill in full, a reception being drinks-led.
2. Where that room stood set for seated rounds and the guests served reach the smallest guest count printed against the package, the seated share of that bar minimum stands on the bill, wine being taken at the table rather than at a full bar. That seated share is 50 per cent of the bar minimum, that is one half of it.
3. Where that room stood set otherwise, or the guests served do not reach the smallest guest count printed against the package, no bar element stands on the bill.

The set-up read here is the room set-up the booking was taken for, as the booking entry records it.

| Package | Bar minimum, USD | Smallest guest count | Reception, USD | Seated rounds, USD |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meeting Room Refreshment Package | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| Boardroom Reception Package | 0 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| Conference Day Delegate Package | 750 | 25 | 750 | 375 |
| Seated Banquet Package | 1800 | 60 | 1800 | 900 |
| Gala Reception Package | 4500 | 150 | 4500 | 2250 |
| Multi-Day Conference Residency Package | 9500 | 200 | 9500 | 4750 |

## Basis questions

*On guests served exactly at the smallest guest count.* Guests served standing at the smallest guest count printed against the package reach it, and the bar element stands.

*On theater, classroom and boardroom set-ups.* No bar element stands on the bill where the booking was taken for any of those rooms, whatever the guests served.
